title: kaizen tool output envelope
description:
Canonical JSON envelope for every kaizen CLI tool's `--json` output. Programmable (predictable shape), reproducible (deterministic ordering, no random ids), consistent (same envelope across every tool). Per-tool payload lives in `data`; envelope metadata in `kaizen`.

Intent: an agent or downstream pipe can call ANY kaizen tool with --json and consume the result via a single shape — `verdict` for go/no-go, `counts` for severity buckets, `data` for the tool-specific payload. New tools opt in by importing `_envelope.py::wrap` and emitting `wrap(...)` instead of bare JSON.

kaizen.description: Envelope metadata — identifies the producing tool + run.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema version. Bump only on breaking shape changes.

tool_version.description: Per-tool semver (independent of plugin version). Omit if the tool has no version.

command.description: Verbatim command line invoked. Useful for reproducibility — paste to re-run.

ran_at_utc.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the tool ran. Optional — omit if reproducibility-by-bit matters (any timestamp breaks byte-identity).

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the tool's run.

verdict.description: High-level go/no-go signal for the run. Pre-defined enums cover gate-style (green/yellow/red), action-style (ok/warn/fail), and audit-style (violated/leaks/clean) verdicts. null for tools that don't produce a verdict (inventory, status).

counts.description: Severity bucket counts. Common keys: error, warn, info. Tool-specific keys allowed.

data.description: Tool-specific payload. Any JSON shape — array, object, primitive. Agents inspect `verdict` + `counts` first, then drill into `data` per the tool's per-tool schema.

errors.description: Tool-internal errors (NOT findings). E.g. "validator subprocess timed out" — communicates partial-run state.
